reason: E2 directly supports the synergistic effect of nanocrystalline microstructure and Y addition on protective scale formation and adhesion. E1 confirms that coarse-grained CrMnFeCoNi forms non-protective Mn-rich oxides, supporting the baseline premise. However, E1 also states that Cr2O3 was not observed, which partially contradicts the mechanism's claim that enhanced Cr diffusion leads to Cr2O3 formation; the hypothesis overstates the role of Cr in this system. E3 is about V-rich oxide evaporation in TiAl alloys and is irrelevant to the key premises.
premises: Nanocrystalline microstructures enhance grain-boundary diffusion of oxide-formers (Cr, Al) to form a continuous protective scale
Trace reactive elements (Y) promote interfacial anchoring of the oxide scale via fine oxide particles
Coarse-grained alloys without reactive elements form discontinuous, non-protective oxides (e.g., Mn-rich) that deplete beneficial elements
The combination of grain refinement and reactive element addition synergistically improves oxidation resistance and material integrity
The CrMnFeCoNi system forms non-protective Mn-rich oxides in the baseline coarse-grained state
